title: Vegetarian Nachos
subtitle: Tortilla chips with black beans, peppers, and melted cheese
excerpt: Tortilla chips piled with spiced black beans, sautéed peppers, and cheddar, baked until the cheese melts, then served with guacamole, soured cream, and jalapeños. Filling, satisfying, and meat-free.
sourceNotes: Vegetarian nachos: a meat-free nacho variation common in US casual restaurants. Black beans replace the beef, giving similar substance and protein without meat. Based on standard American Tex-Mex home-cooking tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bean and pepper filling can be made a day ahead. Assemble and bake just before serving.

content.text: Vegetarian nachos replace the beef with a black bean and pepper filling seasoned with cumin and smoked paprika. The beans hold their shape well in the oven and provide enough substance to make the nachos a proper meal. Cook the peppers separately until the pan is dry before mixing with the beans; wet filling will soften the chips within minutes of coming out of the oven.

items.prepNote: bought tortilla chips, or corn tortillas cut into triangles and baked at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp
mashed with lime juice and salt

content.text: Heat {{olive-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook {{onion}} of finely chopped onion for 4-5 minutes. Add the diced peppers and cook for 4-5 minutes more until softened and lightly charred. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli powder. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the drained black beans and stir through to combine. Season with salt. The filling should be fairly dry with no pooling liquid.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the tortilla chips in a single layer on a large baking tray. Spoon the bean and pepper mixture across the chips. Scatter the grated cheddar over the top.

Bake for 8-10 minutes until the cheese has melted and is beginning to bubble. Remove from the oven. Add the cold toppings: mashed avocado, soured cream, and jalapeño. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

items.cause: Peppers released too much liquid into the filling
items.fix: Cook the peppers until they're well reduced and the pan looks dry. Add the beans last and don't cook them long; they're already cooked and just need warming through.

items.cause: Chips too thin or not enough cheese anchoring the topping
items.fix: Use a generous layer of cheese over the beans. The melted cheese helps the filling adhere. Thicker, ridged tortilla chips hold the topping better than thin ones.

items.cause: Spices not cooked into the vegetables
items.fix: Add the spices to the peppers and onions and cook for 2 full minutes before adding the beans. Spices need heat to bloom and develop flavour.
Mash the avocado just before serving. Add lime juice straight away; the acidity slows browning. Don't prepare it in advance.

content.text: Vegetarian nachos became a standard Tex-Mex restaurant option as the dish expanded in the US from the 1980s. They work because the filling is substantial on its own. Black beans are protein-dense and hold their shape under heat. Spiced beans, charred peppers, and melted cheese together make a complete meal, not just a snack with the meat taken out.
